Shanti’s parents seemed busier planning their summer 
vacation. “Are we doing something different this year?”,

than staying in one place? I really want to see more of

Appa (father) and Amma (mother) smiled, “Shanti, 
your wish might just come true. We have big plans 
this time! A trip to a few different places starting 
from the southernmost tip of India!”.

Some Unique Places
The Northeast of India is a land full of colours, 
creativity and life. People here live closely with nature. 
The region is home to lush forests, flowing rivers, 
and amazing animals and birds. From weaving and 
crafts to music, dance and festivals — every part 
of life is connected to the hills, forests and wildlife 
around them. It is a place where culture and nature 
grow together.
“What are they doing?” I asked.
“What are they doing?”, Shanti asked.
“They are helping protect the Hargila bird, the 
Greater Adjutant Stork”, said Amma. “The women 
are teaching the children to help protect their nests.”
Do you know?
Bhut Jolokia or ghost pepper is one of the hottest 
chillies in the world. It grows in the Northeast India 
and is used in pickles, chutneys, and even to keep 
elephants away from the crops.
The Kailasanatha Temple in Ellora, Maharashtra, is the world’s 
largest building carved from a single rock.

medicine and their livelihood.
Just then, Shanti saw a group of 
students with notebooks and cameras 
under a tree. “What are they doing?”, 
she asked.
“These students are part of a survey. 
With help from schools, farmers and 
experts, we found and recorded over 
200 types of mangoes in the Western 
Ghats! Now, we are also looking 
at jackfruit and jamun”, explained 
Satish, a researcher who was guiding 
the students.
Shanti was amazed. 
“Can I do something like this for the trees and 
fruits in my place too?”, she wondered.

Protected areas are special places like forests, rivers 
or hills that are kept safe by the government to protect 
animals, plants and nature. People are not allowed to 
cut trees or harm animals in these areas. The Western 
Ghats have over 50 protected areas such as, wildlife 
sanctuaries, national parks and tiger reserves. These 
help protect rare animals like the lion-tailed macaque, 
tiger, elephant and hornbill, and keep the forests and 
rivers healthy.
